Indulgent

in-DUL-junt -- three syllables, stress on the second syllable, DUL. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Indulgent is overly generous to or lenient.

The indulgent uncle never said no, buying the children ice cream even when dinner was minutes away.

Worked Example

Every time the puppy chews a shoe, the owner laughs, calls it adorable, and hands over a treat -- and the shoe pile keeps shrinking.

That owner is indulgent -- overly generous and lenient, letting the puppy get away with everything. Indulgent goes past ordinary kindness into excess: giving or permitting more than is good for the one receiving it.

How Indulgent Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

lenient

lenient: mild and permissive rather than strict

pampering

pampering: catering to someone's every comfort

doting

doting: extravagantly and uncritically fond

Antonyms

strict

strict: demanding that rules be followed

stern

stern: severe and firm in manner

How Strong Is It? — lenient → indulgent → doting

lenient vs. indulgent

lenient vs. indulgent: Lenient simply goes easy -- a lenient teacher forgives one late essay -- while indulgent goes further and spoils: an indulgent one would forgive the essay, extend every deadline, and bring snacks to the retake.

doting vs. indulgent

doting vs. indulgent: Doting is about adoring attention, while indulgent is about excess in giving way: doting grandparents can't stop watching the baby, and indulgent ones can't stop handing it cookies.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — indulge-

root — indulge-: to be lenient toward, to give free rein (Latin indulgere)

suffix — -ent

suffix — -ent: in a state of; doing (Latin -entem)

Put it together

Put it together: Indulgent comes straight from Latin indulgere, 'to be kind or lenient toward, to give free rein.' The Romans' word already had the modern flavor: an indulgent person gives way -- kindly, generously, and usually a little too much.

Use the root in a new word: indulge

Use the root in a new word: indulge: On their anniversary, they indulged in a seven-course dinner and ordered dessert twice.

Root Check

Word Choice

Indulgent describes people who allow too much: indulgent parents, an indulgent boss, an indulgent smile at a naughty child. The word always whispers 'more than is wise' -- ordinary generosity gives what is needed, while indulgence gives whatever is wanted.
